milestone: Horizen Pilot — close Standing + MoneyPenny Runtime now; isolate DVN backlog (operator directive, 2026-08-23), P0-A/P0-C/P0-D.
problem: A same-day earlier repair pass (RES-2026-08-23, receipt attribution labeling) fixed `standing_accrued` receipts to correctly LABEL which agent's Standing was credited (`subjectAgentRef`), but left the underlying CREDIT TARGET wrong: `serviceRequestOrchestrator.ts`'s `accrueStandingBestEffort` credited `context.standingPersonaId` — the REQUESTER's own CRM Standing persona, resolved for `request.requestingAgentId` inside `resolveAgentEligibilityContext` — on every successful Financial Services delivery. The PROVIDER (e.g. MoneyPenny), which performed the actual work, never received any Standing credit at all. The operator's own words: 'Successful provider execution accrues contribution Standing to the provider's canonical Standing persona, not to the requester merely for requesting the service.'
observedFailure: Operator live-read of the dev database (correcting this record's initial assumption): three genuinely completed MoneyPenny service interactions exist in the live pilot (`6b5d75b8-69cf-4a8c-9709-8f08bd9e9207` Nakamoto, `3e1e16b2-328a-4a7c-9a07-a1b7a241a8d3` Kn0w1, `0ce6b58f-3b63-4b68-877f-84cb54983280` Nakamoto) — but only ONE erroneous requester-side `standing_accrued` receipt exists (`aae9b6ab-008f-472c-94c6-34b0bdc3b03e`, Nakamoto's own canonical Standing persona). The other two completed interactions produced NO Standing receipt at all — the provider credit was simply never issued, with nothing to reverse.

The Horizen Journey's agent-scoped Standing observer (`resolveStandingEvidence('aigent-moneypenny')`) could never discover contribution evidence for MoneyPenny from any of the three interactions, because no `standing_accrued` receipt was ever written against MoneyPenny's own CRM persona at all.
MoneyPenny has no `aigent-canonical-standing` persona in live dev at all yet — it has never been provisioned.
rootCauses: `accrueStandingBestEffort(context.standingPersonaId, request.requestingAgentId)` was called with the REQUESTER's own resolved eligibility context (`context` is `resolveAgentEligibilityContext(admin, agent, ...)` where `agent` is the requesting agent) — the function was written to credit 'whoever is in scope' rather than deliberately resolving and crediting the PROVIDER (`definition.providerAgentId`), which was never resolved at all in the accrual path prior to this fix.

The earlier same-day attribution-labeling repair (RES-2026-08-23, Fix 1) closed the discoverability gap for whichever persona a receipt already names, but did not re-examine WHICH persona `accrueStanding` was being told to credit in the first place — it fixed the receipt's label to match a still-wrong underlying credit target.
resolution: Rewrote `accrueStandingBestEffort` in `services/financialServices/serviceRequestOrchestrator.ts` to accept `(admin, providerAgentId, requestingAgentId)` and resolve the PROVIDER's own canonical Standing persona via the same canonical chain every other agent Standing resolution in this codebase uses: `resolveRegistrableAgentByRuntimeId(providerAgentId)` -> `resolveAgentAdmissionState(admin, providerAgent)` -> `resolveAgentStandingPersonaId(admin, providerAgent, admission?.agentRootDid)` — idempotently provisioning the provider's `aigent-canonical-standing` persona if it does not yet exist (via `resolveAgentStandingPersonaId`'s existing provisioning logic).

Updated both call sites (post-Advisor/Architect real dispatch; post-execution-bound Runtime) to pass `admin, definition.providerAgentId, request.requestingAgentId` instead of `context.standingPersonaId, request.requestingAgentId`.

Added `requestingAgentRef` to `AccrueStandingInput` (services/crm/standingAccrualService.ts) — recorded ONLY in the receipt's `actionInput`, alongside the existing `orchestratorAgentRef`, and NEVER placed into `agentsInvoked` or substituted for `subjectAgentRef` — preserving the requester as interaction/context evidence, never as the Standing credit recipient.

Built `POST /api/ops/journey/reconcile-provider-standing-attribution` — an idempotent, non-mutating reconciliation for the 3 known pre-fix live interactions. Per the No-Guessing rule, it accepts EXPLICIT `originalReceiptId`s from the operator (no auto-discovery: historical `standing_accrued` receipts carry no reliable structural marker distinguishing a Financial-Services provider-credit from any other legitimate requester accrual). For each: independently re-verifies the receipt genuinely credits the named requester's own canonical identity persona (`RECEIPT_NOT_REQUESTER_CREDITED` refusal otherwise); verifies sequencing validity against the provider's genuine `capability_registered` receipt (`SEQUENCING_INVALID` refusal otherwise); reverses the requester-side credit via `accrueStanding({cvs: -SERVICE_COMPLETION_CVS, ...})` (the exact inverse magnitude, correctly also reversing any sponsor delegated/stewardship side-credit); credits the provider once, genuinely, via an ordinary `accrueStanding({cvs: +SERVICE_COMPLETION_CVS, ...})` call; and writes one additive `standing_corrected` audit receipt (`correctionKind: 'service_completion_reattribution'`) as the idempotency marker for re-runs. Exported `SERVICE_COMPLETION_CVS` from `serviceRequestOrchestrator.ts` so the reversal uses the exact same magnitude constant, never a second independently-guessed one.

Extended `services/financialServices/runtimeReadinessProjection.ts`'s `RuntimeReadinessProjection` with a `systemReady` field — the Runtime pipeline's own operational fact, computed independently of the selected consumer's eligibility/standing/authority, always `ready` today since reaching this projection already implies discovery resolved the service definition and neither Runtime service has an infra dependency beyond Vela (isolated in `confidentialExecution`). Mirrored into the client-side type (`serviceOrchestrationPanelState.ts`) and rendered as its own badge, first, in `ServiceOrchestrationPanel.tsx` — so a consumer refused on Standing/authority/eligibility never visually reads as 'the Runtime is down'.

Extended the reconciliation route additively with a second explicit mode, `BACKFILL_MISSING_PROVIDER_CREDIT`, for the two completed interactions that produced no Standing receipt at all (per the operator's live-DB correction). Given a real `capability_invocation_completed` receipt id, it verifies the receipt genuinely exists and is that action type; verifies the caller-supplied requester/provider against the receipt's OWN `agents_invoked`/`action_input.resolvedProviderId` evidence (never trusting caller-supplied identity alone); verifies sequencing against the provider's genuine `capability_registered` receipt; verifies prior-credit absence via a dedicated idempotency marker (`correctionKind: 'service_completion_provider_backfill'`); and issues the provider's missing credit ONCE via an ordinary positive `accrueStanding` call — never an inverse/reversal accrual (there is no requester credit to reverse) and never a fabricated 'original' `standing_accrued` receipt. The first real credit call is what lets `resolveAgentStandingContext`'s existing provisioning logic idempotently create MoneyPenny's missing `aigent-canonical-standing` persona — no separate provisioning step was added.
rejectedApproaches: Folding the reconciliation's `standing_corrected` audit receipt into `standingEvidenceProjection.ts`'s `effectiveContributionReceipts` set (as the existing `standing_attribution` correction kind already is) — rejected: the reconciliation ALSO calls a genuine, ordinary `accrueStanding()` for the provider, which already writes its own directly-discoverable `standing_accrued` receipt. Counting the audit receipt too would double-count one interaction as two pieces of contribution evidence at the discoverability layer, even though the numeric Standing score is only ever written once — the exact shape of the 'do not duplicate service-completion Standing' defect the operator explicitly warned against, just one layer up from the score itself.

Auto-discovering the 3 known live-pilot receipts by a `cvs === SERVICE_COMPLETION_CVS` numeric match — rejected under the No-Guessing rule: this is a coincidental value match, not proof a given historical receipt was genuinely a Financial-Services provider-credit misattributed to the requester, versus any other legitimate cvs=1 accrual from an unrelated path.

Running REATTRIBUTE for all three completed interactions (the record's own initial assumption, corrected by the operator's live read) — rejected once the live data showed only ONE erroneous requester-side receipt exists; running REATTRIBUTE against the other two would have required fabricating a nonexistent 'original' receipt to reverse, which this route must never do.

Issuing the two missing provider credits via the REATTRIBUTE code path with a null/skipped reversal step — rejected in favor of a distinct, explicit mode (`BACKFILL_MISSING_PROVIDER_CREDIT`) with its own verification shape (completed-interaction evidence, not a standing_accrued receipt) and its own idempotency marker, so the two defect shapes ('wrong credit target' vs 'missing credit entirely') stay structurally distinguishable rather than one code path silently branching on the absence of a step.
unresolvedRisks: The reconciliation route has not been invoked live — this sandbox has no live Supabase credentials. The operator must run one REATTRIBUTE correction (`aae9b6ab-008f-472c-94c6-34b0bdc3b03e`) and two BACKFILL_MISSING_PROVIDER_CREDIT corrections (`6b5d75b8-69cf-4a8c-9709-8f08bd9e9207`, `3e1e16b2-328a-4a7c-9a07-a1b7a241a8d3`) before MoneyPenny's genuine contribution Standing reflects in production.
The 3,323-message DVN backlog is explicitly out of scope for this pass per the operator's own instruction, and remains a separate, unresolved infrastructure incident.
